input.question: What is the reason for morning sickness and other"symptoms" in pregnant women? What, if any, are the advantages to us as a species?
input.ground_truth: (Biologist) Pregnancy sickness prevents the mother ingesting harmful toxins that could damage the embryo. As the embryo is developing (internal organs, limbs etc.) it is incredibly sensitive to toxins that would usually have no effect, e.g. asparagus is fatal to hamster embryos but is a perfectly suitable food for adults. Pregnancy sickness causes retching when these toxins (usually bitter tasting) are detected. It is incredibly useful: women who experience pregnancy sickness (about 75%) are half as likely to have a miscarriage than women who don't.

Okay, let’s imagine your tummy is like a little house where a tiny new baby is growing. Sometimes, when the baby is very small, your tummy can get a little upset and you might feel sick in the morning or have other funny feelings. This is called morning sickness.

It happens because the baby is making some changes inside your body, and your body is getting used to the new baby. It’s kind of like when you get a new toy and you’re so excited and a little bit nervous at the same time.

Now, for our species (that means people like us!), having these feelings might actually help the baby stay safe. The sickness might make some women eat different foods or avoid things that could hurt the baby. So, it’s like your body is protecting the baby by saying, “Hey, let’s be careful what we eat right now!”

So, morning sickness and those funny feelings can help keep the baby healthy while it grows. That’s good for the baby and for all of us in the future!
